records.title: The problem

records.core_message: The current market for business software is fragmented, forcing businesses to choose between commoditized payment processors, narrow niche software, or poorly integrated roll-ups of acquired companies.

shows.specific_content: A three-panel slide describing flawed industry approaches. The first panel, 'Commodity Payments,' shows a generic credit card. The second, 'Niche Software,' shows a food bowl with an 'Order Now' button. The third, 'Disjointed M&A Roll-Up,' shows scattered puzzle pieces that don't fit together.
shows.data_points_shown: No quantitative data is shown. The slide uses conceptual labels and representative images to categorize market players.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern establishes a problem by categorizing the competitive landscape into distinct, flawed archetypes. It typically presents 2-3 common but suboptimal approaches in an industry (e.g., the basic commodity, the narrow point solution, the fragmented conglomerate). Any company can use this to frame their own solution as the superior, integrated alternative that overcomes the weaknesses of the status quo. It effectively creates a 'Goldilocks' problem where existing options are 'too simple,' 'too narrow,' or 'too messy,' setting the stage for the 'just right' solution.
works_for: The marketing tech landscape is a mess of point solutions that don't talk to each other.
Traditional banks are slow and outdated, while new fintech apps lack a full suite of services.
Companies either rely on generic HR software or a messy combination of specialized tools for payroll, benefits, and recruiting.
Existing BI tools are either too simple for data teams or too complex for business users.
Cloud security is addressed by a patchwork of tools for identity, network, and data, creating security gaps.
You can either hire expensive consultants or use rigid, off-the-shelf software, but neither truly fits your workflow.
Current project management tools are either simple to-do lists or overly complex enterprise systems.

data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 2-3 distinct competitor archetypes or flawed approaches.

variable_elements.secondary_metric: The composition of the primary metric by source (e.g., product line, customer segment, geography, business model)

Showing that the business is becoming more defensible and diversified.

Your overall growth is flat or declining, as this would undermine the transformation story.

works_for: Our revenue is shifting from one-off projects to recurring subscriptions.

Our free users are increasingly converting to our premium paid tiers over time.
Our business has transformed from being hardware-centric to software-driven.

variable_elements.secondary_metric: A customer segmentation based on engagement level (e.g., number of products used, subscription tier, user tenure).
variable_elements.time_dimension: A multi-period time series (e.g., years, quarters).
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time, showing internal transformation.

Ability to segment the customer base by their level of product adoption or engagement.
Data linked at the individual customer level over time.

ideal_for: Proving that a 'land-and-expand' or platform strategy is creating more valuable customers.
Demonstrating a successful business model transformation to investors.
Showing that the customer base is becoming higher quality and more locked-in.
Justifying R&D investment in building a multi-product ecosystem.
Highlighting the growing moat around your business.
When moving upmarket, to show the growing contribution from larger customers.
avoid_when: You are a single-product company.
Your data does not show a clear, positive shift in customer adoption or value.
You lack several years of historical data to build the trend.

Updating investors on progress against a long-term strategic plan.

Your market size has remained flat or shrunk.

Explaining to stakeholders why a particular strategic direction was chosen.
Justifying investment in a product area by showing its growing market adoption.

If your own company's growth is significantly lagging the market trend shown.

variable_elements.secondary_metric: Categories of behavior or technology

Instead of the company stating its own benefits, the customer explains in their own words how the product solves a real problem and drives a tangible outcome (e.g., growth, efficiency, insight). This approach builds credibility and creates an emotional connection, translating abstract features into a relatable success story. Any company can use this to prove its product's real-world impact.
works_for: Our CRM helps sales teams automate follow-ups, giving them more time to sell.
Our developer platform cuts down build times, allowing engineering teams to ship faster.
This financial planning app gave me the clarity to finally start saving for a house.
Using this logistics software, we were able to reduce our shipping errors by 90%.
Our security product gives our CISO peace of mind about our cloud infrastructure.
This learning platform has transformed how our employees develop new skills.
With this marketing tool, we can finally attribute revenue to specific campaigns.

variable_elements.primary_metric: Qualitative customer testimonial
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicit before-and-after using the product

must_have: An articulate, benefit-focused customer quote
Permission from the customer to use their name, title, company, and likeness
A high-quality photograph of the customer or their business environment
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: A specific, narrative quote that connects a product feature to a positive business or personal outcome.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 1 strong customer story

To prove your product's value proposition in a more compelling way than a feature list.
To illustrate a specific use case that resonates with a target customer segment.
When transitioning from 'what' your product does to 'why' it matters to users.
To break up a series of dense, data-heavy slides with an emotional, relatable story.
In an investor pitch to show you have happy, referenceable customers.
avoid_when: When you don't have a strong, specific quote that reinforces your narrative.
If you don't have permission or a high-quality image, as a poor execution undermines credibility.
When you have no happy, referenceable customers yet.

variable_elements.secondary_metric: A measure of recent progress, such as 'number of new products launched'.
variable_elements.time_dimension: Implicitly shown by comparing 'new' vs 'existing' components, not a time-series.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Comparison across different segments (e.g., countries) against a benchmark segment (e.g., most mature country).

Illustrating a 'land and expand' strategy across geographies or customer segments.
Justifying investment in less mature markets by showing a clear path to parity with a successful one.
Demonstrating the scalability and replicability of a product ecosystem or business model.
Showing investors a large, untapped opportunity within your existing footprint.
avoid_when: You are only in one market or customer segment.
Your product offering is identical and fully penetrated across all segments.
Your growth story is about creating entirely new products for all markets, not expanding existing ones.

variable_elements.primary_metric: An absolute value for a specific business segment (e.g., Gross Profit, Revenue, Active Users, GMV).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: The segment's metric as a percentage of the company's total for that same metric.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: A business segment's growth over time, shown both in absolute terms and as a growing percentage of the whole business.

must_have: Time-series data for a key metric (e.g., revenue, profit) for a specific business segment.
Time-series data for the same metric for the total business to calculate the percentage share.
Breakdown of the segment's metric into at least 2-3 sub-components (e.g., regions, sub-products).

data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 4-5+ time periods (e.g., years) to show a convincing trend, and 2+ sub-components for the stacked chart.

ideal_for: Proving a new growth strategy (like international expansion or moving upmarket) is working.
Highlighting a fast-growing part of the business to show diversification and future potential.
Justifying increased investment in a particular segment or market.
Showing investors that the company has multiple engines of growth.
Demonstrating successful market penetration in new geographies or customer verticals.
Answering the question 'What's your next big growth driver?'
avoid_when: The segment's growth is slow, flat, or declining.
The segment is still an insignificant fraction of the total business (e.g., <1%) after several years.
Growth is highly concentrated in one sub-component, suggesting a lack of broad-based traction.

records.core_message: Our platform can serve even the most remote and challenging markets that traditional systems cannot reach, demonstrating our unique capabilities and expansive market opportunity.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern uses a compelling narrative and evocative imagery to introduce a difficult, seemingly unsolvable customer problem. It establishes a specific, challenging scenario (e.g., a remote location, a complex industry, a highly regulated environment) where traditional solutions fail. This sets the stage for the company's product to be presented as the unique hero or solution, thereby proving its superior capability, flexibility, or reach. Scientists in field research had no way to process large datasets without access to high-performance computing.

variable_elements.secondary_metric: The 'Reason' for the failure of traditional solutions (e.g., complexity, location, regulation).

High-quality photos or visuals that illustrate the customer's environment and challenges
A clear, concise problem statement

data_requirements.minimum_data_points: One strong, well-documented customer case study.

To humanize your technology and show its real-world impact on a specific community or business.
As an introduction to a detailed case study that will showcase product benefits.
To demonstrate the breadth of your total addressable market by including underserved segments.
To build an emotional connection with the audience before diving into technical details or metrics.
When you want to show your solution is not just for mainstream customers but can handle edge cases.
avoid_when: When you need to show quantitative data and trends across your entire user base.
In a very short pitch where you don't have time for narrative storytelling.
If the story isn't genuinely compelling or doesn't clearly differentiate you from competitors.

Building credibility with investors about execution risk.
Illustrating the real-world impact of your product beyond simple metrics.
Showcasing successful partnerships with major entities like governments.

You lack high-quality, authentic visuals to support the story.
The case study is not significant enough to warrant a dedicated slide.

shows.specific_content: Two smartphone mockups displaying the UI for Square Checking and Square Savings accounts, alongside a large callout statistic stating that over 15% of Gross Payment Volume (GPV) from large sellers (>$125K annualized GPV) is stored in Square savings accounts.
shows.data_points_shown: Key stat: >15% of GPV stored in savings. Customer segment: Sellers with >$125K annualized GPV. Example UI balances: $24,678.43 in checking, $1,850.00 in savings.

records.abstract_pattern: Any company can use this pattern to prove deep product integration and user trust. It works by first showing tangible product screenshots to ground the audience in the user experience. This is then immediately reinforced by a single, powerful 'hero' statistic that quantifies deep engagement for a specific, high-value customer segment. The key is connecting product usage (e.g., assets stored, workflows managed) to a core business value driver (e.g., revenue, transaction volume), demonstrating that the product is not just a feature but a central part of the user's life or business.
works_for: Our top creators earn over 50% of their income directly through our platform's monetization tools.
Enterprise customers run over 75% of their critical workflows on our project management software.
Our average B2B customer centralizes 90% of their vendor payments through our system.
More than 60% of our active users have connected their primary bank account for seamless investing.
Our power users spend 4+ hours per day inside our design application.
Our data platform manages over 80% of our clients' total customer data.
The majority of our restaurant clients use our platform for both online ordering and in-house inventory.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A ratio or percentage showing deep engagement (e.g., % of revenue stored, % of time spent, % of workflows managed).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A definition of the high-value customer segment (e.g., users with >$X in revenue, enterprise-tier customers).
variable_elements.time_dimension: A point-in-time snapshot or a recent period average.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicitly measures the share of a user's activity captured by the platform versus being done externally.

must_have: Product usage data (e.g., savings balance, features used)
A core business metric for the same users (e.g., GPV, revenue, total spend)
A way to segment users by value or size
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a strong correlation between a high-value customer segment and deep adoption of a specific product, resulting in a compelling percentage or ratio.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: Data from a statistically significant number of users within the target segment over a defined period (e.g., 3-6 months).

ideal_for: Proving a new product is gaining significant traction with your most important customers.
Demonstrating your platform's 'stickiness' and how it creates a competitive moat.
Showing your product is becoming the central 'system of record' or financial hub for users.
Illustrating the concept of 'share of wallet' or 'share of workflow'.
Justifying further investment in a product line by showing its current success.
When moving from a single-point solution to a multi-product platform.
avoid_when: The adoption metric is low and doesn't sound impressive (e.g., <5%).
You cannot tie product usage to a specific, high-value customer segment.
The product is a simple, non-critical feature rather than core to the user's workflow.

records.abstract_pattern: Any company can use this pattern to prove the value of a specific feature, program, or product tier. It works by segmenting the user base into two groups: those who have adopted the feature ('engaged') and those who have not ('unengaged'). The slide then presents a side-by-side comparison of a key performance metric (like spend, retention, or usage) for these two groups. The goal is to show a clear, positive uplift for the engaged segment, providing concrete evidence that the feature drives desirable business outcomes and has a strong ROI.
works_for: Our premium subscribers have 3x higher engagement than free users.
Customers who use our mobile app order 50% more frequently than web-only customers.
Users who complete our onboarding checklist are 70% more likely to retain after 90 days.

Students who join study groups on our platform have 20% higher course completion rates.

variable_elements.secondary_metric: A composition metric showing the mix of users or revenue (e.g., % of Sales, % of Users).
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Comparison between two internal user segments (e.g., engaged vs. unengaged, premium vs. free).

must_have: Ability to segment customers based on feature adoption or program membership (e.g., loyalty vs. non-loyalty).
A key performance metric (e.g., average spend, LTV, retention) for each customer segment.
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: needs clear contrast/difference
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 2 customer segments with 1 comparable metric

ideal_for: Proving the ROI of a specific feature or add-on product.
Justifying a premium pricing tier by showing its tangible value.
Demonstrating how product features drive customer stickiness and retention.
Making the case for up-selling or cross-selling a feature to your existing customer base.
Showing investors how product development creates measurable financial impact.
avoid_when: The feature has no measurable or a negative impact on key metrics.
You cannot clearly segment your users based on feature adoption.
The uplift is too small to be meaningful or convincing.

Our value creation starts with a world-class user experience.

variable_elements.secondary_metric: The first or foundational component of the framework (e.g., 'Remarkable Products', 'Community', 'Data Asset').

Our growth comes from a virtuous cycle of data network effects and product innovation.
Our business model has two pillars: a sticky core product and a scalable distribution channel.

As a title slide for a section detailing your product and marketing synergy.
